chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, and others, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' He said: 'It is not for the two judges to effect separation until they are instructed for it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the role of the two judges in resolving marital discord according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies the procedural limitation of the two arbiters mentioned in Quran 4:35, stating they cannot unilaterally effect separation (*Tafreeq*) without first seeking confirmation or deliberation (*Istiamara*). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the arbiters' role is primarily conciliatory and investigative, requiring a decisive basis before dissolving the marriage bond. The emphasis on *Istiamara* underscores the caution required in marital dispute resolution to prevent hasty or unjust separation.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, and someone else, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws), said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:35] then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for the two judges that they effect separation until they are instructed for it’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah and others from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about, ‘If you are afraid of discord between them then send one arbitrator from his people and another from her people.’ [4:35]
He (the Imam) said, ‘They cannot decide to separate them without previous authorization of their decision by the parties (the wife and husband).’
